issues.legal_issue: A purchaser seeking specific performance of an agreement for reconveyance need not make a formal tender of the purchase money when the vendor has unequivocally repudiated the agreement and would have refused payment.
material_facts: The agreement required the purchaser to pay the agreed price by a specified deadline in return for a conveyance of the property.
Before the deadline, the purchaser’s solicitor said the purchaser was ready and willing to complete and sent a draft conveyance.
The vendor’s solicitors denied that any concluded or valid agreement existed.
The purchaser did not formally tender the purchase money before filing suit for specific performance.
issues.conclusion: Because the vendor had unequivocally repudiated the agreement, a formal tender would have been a useless formality, and the purchaser could obtain a decree for specific performance without making one.
issues.legal_principle: Under Hunter v. Daniel (1845) 4 Hare 420 and Chalikani Venkatarayanim v. Zamindar of Tuni (1922) L.R. 50 I.A. 41, a court does not require formal tender when the facts show that the recipient would have refused the money. The relevant question is whether there was a clear refusal to perform and an intimation that payment would be refused, not whether the purchaser had the money within their power. No statutory provision is relied on.

rule.if: specific_performance_proceeding and purchaser_communicated_readiness_to_pay and vendor_unequivocally_repudiated and no_formal_tender

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: A purchaser brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of an agreement for reconveyance or sale.
predicates.purchaser_communicated_readiness_to_pay: The purchaser, personally or through a representative, communicated readiness to pay the agreed price and complete the transaction.
predicates.vendor_unequivocally_repudiated: The vendor clearly denied the agreement or otherwise refused to perform it.
predicates.no_formal_tender: The purchaser did not formally tender the agreed price.

issues.definition: When a purchaser seeking specific performance communicates readiness to pay but does not formally tender the price, an unequivocal repudiation by the vendor permits specific performance to be decreed without formal tender.

issues.legal_issue: An offer to perform a contractual payment obligation is not invalid merely because the purchaser communicates it through a solicitor acting as the purchaser’s agent.
material_facts: In a suit for specific performance of an agreement for reconveyance, the purchaser’s solicitor wrote to the vendor seeking completion and communicating that the purchaser was ready to pay the agreed price.
The solicitor also sent a draft conveyance for approval.
The vendor disputed that the agreement existed.
issues.conclusion: An offer made through a solicitor acting as an agent can be a proper offer in law; it is not invalid merely because it was made through the solicitor.
issues.legal_principle: The Court rejected the contention that a solicitor’s offer was not a proper offer in law, observing that a solicitor is an agent for that purpose. Ismail Bhai Rahim v. Adam Osman, I.L.R. [1938] 2 Cal. 337, was distinguished; it concerned whether an offer to pay a debt with interest gave the promisee a reasonable opportunity to ascertain the promisor’s ability and willingness to perform. No statutory provision is relied on.

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: A purchaser brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of a contract.
predicates.solicitor_acting_for_purchaser_communica: A solicitor acting for the purchaser communicated an offer to perform the purchaser’s contractual obligation.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance proceeding, an offer communicated by the purchaser’s solicitor acting as agent is not invalid merely because it was communicated through the solicitor.
